The demo, on paper

A screen-by-screen walk through the Influencer Impact Dashboard — so you can present it with confidence even without the live app open. The screenshots are the real product; follow the talking points under each one.

Read this before you present

Sample data. The influencers shown (Nova Reels, Ghost Grid, Spike Steele…) are fabricated for demonstration — not real people. The app and its analytics are fully real and working; only the underlying numbers are illustrative until a live data vendor is connected. Safe to show anyone.

01

The board that replaces the spreadsheet

On screen

Every influencer the agency tracks — across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube — ranked by median (typical) views, not average. Green tags are genuinely consistent performers; red tags are accounts that look big but aren't.

Say this

“This one screen replaces the 50-tab spreadsheet. The top of the list is who actually moves the needle. And notice number seven — Ghost Grid — half a million followers, ranked dead last and flagged red.”

The point

Followers lie; median reach doesn't. The ranking, the tiers, and the red/green signal are all computed by the app.

02

Why we rank by median, not average

On screen

One influencer's detail. The big number is the median; the small “mean” beneath it is shown only for comparison. The chart is his last ten posts.

Say this

“On average Spike looks like a 250-thousand-view TikToker. But look — one post went viral at 2.4 million; the other nine sit around twelve thousand. The dashed line is the average, dragged up by that one hit. The gold line — the median — is where he really lives.”

The point

Median 12.5K vs. mean 251K — the app caught a 20× inflation. Averages lie; the median tells the truth.

03

Catching a follower-rich ghost

On screen

The most extreme case — an account carried entirely by one lucky post. The table shows seven posts with no views at all, and one that hit 780K.

Say this

“Five hundred thousand followers, and the app ranks the reach at zero. Because that's the reality — nine dead posts and one fluke. This is the client's nightmare: paying an influencer who's really a ghost.”

The point

Exposed in seconds. (Note: Instagram doesn't report shares, so the app simply leaves them out — it never guesses a number.)

04

The booking decision, side by side

On screen

Line up any candidates on their median numbers. The strongest median reach is highlighted; the inflated account is obvious.

Say this

“When you're deciding who to book, you compare what matters — typical reach, not a follower count or a flattering average. Nova Reels wins on median; the ghost is plain to see.”

The point

Turns “who should we book?” into a one-glance answer.

After the walkthrough

What it takes to make this real

Everything in this deck runs today. The dashboard, the median-first ranking, the outlier flags, the charts — all built and working. The only thing between this demo and a client's real influencers is one dependency.

The one dependency

A licensed data feed that returns, per influencer, the last ~20 posts with a view count on every post. Plug it in and the exact screens in this deck fill with the client's real influencers — no rebuild.

Full detail, vendor options and cost are in the companion brief, “What it takes to run on real data.”

There's also an operator mode (behind a login) to pull fresh data, import a spreadsheet, recompute, and export — not shown here to keep the walkthrough to the client-facing views.
